title: buffer-curve-ordering-heuristic-and-utilization-scenario-sheet
summary: Working spreadsheet for a demand-driven ordering heuristic: ties safety-buffer sizing to observed utilization curves per region and dynamically suggests order quantities and fallback lanes. Intended for short-to-mid runway (6-26 weeks) and to feed procurement batch windows.
purpose: Create a repeatable, parametric ordering playbook that (a) reduces excess SKU concentration, (b) keeps per-region runway >= X weeks under stress scenarios, and (c) exposes when to exercise short-term lease/spot channels.
assumptions: Burn = active inference tokens translated to effective GPU-hours using latest CV/LLM mixes
Lead times: standard factory orders 12-18 weeks; channel/third-party lease 1-6 weeks
Region demand growth scenarios: baseline 8% qtr, spike 30% event-triggered
Substitution matrix: newer A100-class SKU can replace older V100 at 0.9 perf ratio for most workloads
Planned maintenance and depot holdback = 6% of fleet capacity
safety_buffer_curve_description: Safety buffer % = base_buffer + (utilization_pct - target_util_pct) * sensitivity_factor + lead_time_weeks * LT_factor. Base_buffer defaults to 12%. Target_util_pct = 68%. sensitivity_factor = 0.35 (per 10% util delta -> +3.5%). LT_factor = 1.8% per week.
how_to_use: 1) Input region / SKU burn and on-hand. 2) Select scenario (baseline / surge / lease-loss). 3) Review suggested next-order qty and holdback lanes. 4) Mark orders for commit window and tag fallback lanes (short-leases, cross-region transfers).
scenario_notes: us-east-1 row flagged: runway < 6 weeks under baseline -> priority order and move to dedicated procurement lane (requires finance approval for accelerated freight).
ap-southeast-1 has long lead time for H100s; recommended split order: 60% long-lead factory commit, 40% short-term lease to cover 6-12 week gap.
ca-central-1 shows surplus relative to local burn; mark 40 units for potential cross-region transfer to us-east if transfer cost < 12% unit price.
decision_log: 2024-10-20: Adopted LT_factor = 1.8% after SRE stress-test; rationale: covers maintenance and shipping variability.
2024-10-25: Sensitivity_factor reduced from 0.5 to 0.35 to avoid over-ordering during transient bursts.
2024-11-02: Agreed to reserve a 6% depot holdback across all regions for immediate OTS replacement.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: SKU-specific supply shock (e.g., H100 allocation re-prioritized) -> Mitigation: maintain two compatible substitution SKUs and pre-approved lease provider list.
Risk: Transport delay spikes from APAC ports -> Mitigation: increase local short-lease buffer and reweight orders toward OEM-direct with earlier commit windows.
Risk: Unexpected demand spike from large customer -> Mitigation: auto-trigger canary order path (20% addl) and notify commercial to throttle or monetize premium queue.
short_run_actions: Place us-east-1 A100-80GB expedited purchase (480 units suggested) in next bid window; finance to approve expedited freight by 2024-11-12.
Open 3 short-lease contracts for ap-southeast-1 H100 (target coverage 40% of predicted 12-week gap).
Inventory team to validate physical counts for us-west-1 and ca-central-1 by 2024-11-05.
longer_run_recs: Introduce a quarterly SKU consolidation review: retire low-utilization SKUs where substitution ratio > 0.85 and savings > 6% ops cost.
Negotiate staggered shipment clauses with OEMs to allow partial delivery and reallocation across regions without penalty.
Automate runway alerts in the procurement dashboard: alert when est weeks runway < (lead_time_weeks + 4).
notes_for_procurement: When approving suggested quantities, prioritize (1) reducing cross-sku concentration, (2) minimizing rush freight exposure, (3) preserving ability to reallocate units across regions within 6 weeks. Use suggested orders as guidance, not hard commits—exceptions must be recorded in procurement backlog.
appendix_examples: Example calc for us-east-1: utilization 74% -> util_delta = 6% -> util_component = 0.35 * 0.6 = 0.21% (normalized per 1% -> 0.21%), lead_time 16w -> LT_component = 16 * 1.8% = 28.8%, base 12% -> safety_buffer ≈ 12 + 0.21 + 28.8 = 41.01% (round to 41%).
Rationale: high safety buffer triggered mainly by long lead time; short-leases recommended to smooth arrival.
Swap rule: if primary SKU cannot be delivered in 12 weeks, auto-offer substitution with perf ratio >= 0.9 and pre-approved firmware/driver images.
